question: The ratio of the cost prices of articles X and Y is 3 : 7. A man earns a profit of 14% by selling X and loses 11% by selling Y. What is his gain/loss percentage in the entire transaction?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Apply the weighted average method to find the net profit or loss percentage directly.

Net Profit/Loss % = [(Ratio of X × Profit % on X) + (Ratio of Y × Loss % on Y)] ÷ (Sum of Ratios)

⇒ Net % = [(3 × 14) + (7 × −11)] ÷ (3 + 7)

⇒ Net % = (42 − 77) ÷ 10 = −35 ÷ 10 = −3.5%

The negative sign indicates a net loss of 3.5% in the entire transaction.

**∴ The correct answer is Loss, 3.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of Cost Prices of articles X and Y = 3 : 7

Profit earned on article X = 14%

Loss incurred on article Y = 11%
